session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: To what extent do you support or oppose universal healthcare policies that provide government-funded healthcare coverage for all citizens? Please explain your reasoning.
column3: I would be in support of universal health care policies that provide coverage for all citizens because health is the most important thing in our life. And without it, we can be faced with a lot of difficulties and problems. People should feel comfortable knowing that this is something that could be provided to them in the event that they really need the health care.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: What do you think are the most significant impacts, positive or negative, of implementing a universal healthcare system?
column3: The most significant positive impact is citizens knowing that they are protected in case something goes wrong and that they have access to healthcare. A significant negative impact would be potential increases in taxes to cover the costs.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: How do you think universal healthcare policies might affect healthcare quality and accessibility?
column3: Health care policies could potentially impact quality and accessibility if everyone has health care now and there's not enough providers. It could make wait times longer and appointments harder to obtain.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: What impact do you believe a universal healthcare system might have on medical innovation and research?
column3: It could make innovation and research a top priority since more people are in need of healthcare, they need to make sure that enough research is being done to give people more opportunities and options when it comes to their healthcare.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: How do you think universal healthcare might affect the economic burden on individuals and families?
column3: Since a good percentage of people probably don't have health care and now there is more to accommodate for, there could be an economic burden if more people have to pay taxes to cover this new government policy, which can be very expensive.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: What role do you believe government should play in healthcare delivery and financing?
column3: I believe the government should allow healthcare to all individuals so that people can live a life in comfort knowing that they will be taken care of if something goes wrong.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: How might healthcare provider concerns factor into decisions about universal healthcare implementation?
column3: I think healthcare provider concerns would be if there's enough space to accommodate more people, more healthcare facilities will need to be built in order to maintain new patients and regular checkups for more people.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: What economic effects, both positive and negative, might result from transitioning to a universal healthcare system?
column3: Not only will more people need healthcare, but more facilities will need to be built to accommodate more people, so it can be a lot of costs in order for this to happen.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: How do you think the interests of taxpayers versus healthcare consumers should be balanced when making healthcare policy?
column3: I think in order for the healthcare policy to go into effect, it should apply to all taxpayers and if someone isn't paying taxes, then they probably shouldn't have as much access to the free healthcare since they are not participating at all.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: What role do you think social equity and access to care play in discussions about healthcare policy?
column3: I think social equity is important in discussions about health care policy so that everything is created in a fair manner so that everyone can participate but also make sure that it doesn't affect anyone in a negative way.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: Is the effect of Access to healthcare on Support for universal healthcare immediate, or does it take time to develop? Does it have a positive effect (increasing it) or a negative effect (decreasing it)? How strong is this effect?
column3: I think this would take time to develop because there may be some time for people to learn and understand the new policy and how it can benefit them. There can definitely be a positive effect if more people know they have access to healthcare when they need it.

session_1758604640281_7rtbya7: What factors do you think influence Support for universal healthcare, and how strong is their impact? Please also indicate if these influences are positive (increasing) or negative (decreasing).
column3: I think the factors that influence support for universal healthcare are lack of resources for most people. If more people had access to healthcare, it would make them in favor of the universal healthcare. If people have special health needs, it would also be a factor knowing that they can be taken care of without having to worry about large bills and expenses.
